info.title: Holo Player HTTP API
info.summary: Everything a Holo Player board does, over Wi-Fi: its files, screen, lights, holoprojector, scenes, settings, network and firmware.
info.description:
The board serves this API on port 80 of every interface it has: its address on your network, `<hostname>.local` (mDNS, by default `holo-xxxx.local`), and `192.168.4.1` on its own access point (`wifi ap on`). The same file is served by the board at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, and always describes the firmware serving it.

This document's `version` is the API's, not the firmware's: `/api/v1/info` reports the firmware version, and the path's `v1` changes only when an existing client would break.

**Protection.** Reading is always open. A request that changes something (`PUT`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) must carry the board's address or name in its `Host` header, and a `POST` or `PATCH` must be `Content-Type: application/json`; together these stop a web page elsewhere from driving the board. Pages from a short list of trusted sites -- Swagger Editor, `astromech.co` and `davidiansmith.ca` with their subdomains, changed with `web cors` on the console -- may call the API from a browser: the board answers their CORS preflights. When a password is set on the board (`web password <password>` on its console), those requests -- and downloading a file, and reading the web settings -- also need it, as `Authorization: Bearer <password>` or HTTP Basic with any user name.

**Updates** are a session: an image is received (uploaded or pulled) into the slot that is not running, checked by the board, and *staged*. Activating makes it the boot image; it runs from the next restart, on trial until it is up, when it confirms itself. Until an image is activated, nothing changes what the board boots.

**Now, and from now on.** Some resources are what the board is doing *now* -- `/screen`, `/leds`, `/holo`, the servos' positions -- and change nothing that survives a restart. Others are *saved*: `/settings`, `/scenes`, a servo's calibration and drive policy, `/network`'s known networks and access point, and `/web`. What the board does when it starts is `settings.boot_scene`: a scene, applied after the saved backlight and LED brightness.

**Shapes.** What the board is doing now is read with `GET` and changed with `PATCH`: send only the fields that change; the reply is the whole new state. Actions are `POST` with a JSON body. Saved, named things -- a scene, a servo's calibration, a known network -- are `PUT` and `DELETE`, named in the query (`?name=`, `?id=`, `?ssid=`).

**Files** are named by a `path` query parameter, from the root of the board's storage: `/clips/intro.mov`. `/` is the root; `..`, `.` and empty segments are refused, as are names over 63 bytes and paths over 159. Moving, replacing or deleting the file on the screen stops it first.

**Long operations** -- an upload or pull of firmware, a file upload, download or copy, a SHA-256, a Wi-Fi scan -- run one at a time; another gets `409 busy`. The server answers other requests meanwhile.

**Events.** Rather than polling, a client can follow `GET /api/v1/events`, a stream of Server-Sent Events: each resource (`screen`, `leds`, `holo`, the running `scene`, ...) as it changes, and what happens (`clip_ended`, `scene_ended`, `touch`). A browser's `EventSource` reconnects by itself and replays what it missed.

**The host link.** Most of this API is also served over a wire, to a controller on the board's spare pins: one request a line, with the same paths, bodies, replies and errors (`/link` has its settings; the manual's *Host link protocol* page has the line format). There, no password or `Host` rule applies. *Planned: not in the firmware yet.*

With a `slot`, the image already in it: naming the other slot goes back to the previous firmware, and naming the running slot undoes an activation that has not restarted yet. The board checks the image before selecting it. `reboot` defaults to true: the board restarts a second after replying.

post.summary: Have the board download an image itself
post.description: From `url` -- an application image, or a release manifest (`.../firmware/manifest.json` on the documentation site), whose SHA-256 is then enforced -- or from a release `channel` such as `latest`, looked up on the documentation site. The download runs in the background: the reply comes once it has started, and `GET /api/v1/ota/image` follows it. Redirects from https to plain http are refused. Needs the board's station link to the internet.

get.summary: Follow what changes: a stream of Server-Sent Events
get.description:
With `Accept: text/event-stream` (what a browser's `EventSource` sends), the reply is a stream that stays open: each event is an SSE `event:` line naming it, and a `data:` line holding it as JSON, a StateEvent or a Happening. A happening's `seq` is also its `id:`, so a reconnecting `EventSource` sends `Last-Event-ID` and gets what it missed, if the board still has it. States are not replayed: read them again with their GETs after a reconnect. Every 15 s a stream gets `system` or, if it didn't ask for that, a comment line, so a client that went away is noticed.

Without `Accept: text/event-stream`, or with `format=json`, the reply is the kept happenings as JSON, for a client that polls.

A few streams can be open at once (3 unless the firmware is built otherwise); one more gets `503` `busy`.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated: only these kinds. Every kind without it. An unknown kind is `400`

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Start with the kept happenings after this `seq` (0: every kept one). The `Last-Event-ID` header does the same

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The kept happenings as JSON, whatever `Accept` says

200.description: The stream, or the kept happenings

get.summary: The host link: its settings, what is running, its counters

patch.description: Saved. A new `mode`, `pins`, `attn`, `i2c_address` or `general_call` waits for a restart, and the reply says so with `restart_required`; the rest applies at once. Over the link itself, a new `baud` takes effect after the reply, which is sent at the old one.

409.description: A pin is one the board uses for something else

get.summary: The happenings the link hasn't given its host yet
get.description: The happenings of the link's kinds not yet given to its host, oldest first; over the link, they then count as given. Over HTTP, this only looks. To catch up after a gap in `seq`, use `GET /events?after=`.

patch.summary: The events the link reports, until the next restart
patch.description: Not saved: `PATCH /link` with `events` sets what it reports from the start.

auth.description: Whether a password is set: changes need it

boots.description: The boot image: runs after a restart

state.description: The bootloader's record: `trial` runs until it confirms itself; null when there is no record (an image installed over USB)

Session.description: The update in progress, or the last one this boot

state.description: `receiving` (an upload or the console) or `downloading` (a pull); `verifying` while the board checks the whole image; `staged` checked and waiting; `active` the boot image, running from the next restart; `failed` with `error`. The running image boots in every state but `active`.

url.description: For a pull: the image's URL, once resolved

sha256.description: Of the image as received, once complete

app.description: Known from the image's first 288 bytes

rollback.description: Updated images run on trial, and a reset before they confirm goes back

slot.description: A slot's label; the staged image when absent

url.description: An image, or a release manifest (ending .json)

channel.description: A release channel: a documentation version or alias

sha256.description: Refuse the image unless it has this SHA-256 (a manifest's own is used otherwise)

force.description: Accept an image built for another project

version.description: The release's version; null for a bare image URL

newer.description: Whether `version` is a later release than `current`; null when either is not a release tag

root.description: Where the volume is mounted on the board; paths here are relative to it

mtime.description: When it last changed, in UTC; null when the board's clock was not set then

entries.description: Directories first, then files, each by name

to.description: The new path. An existing directory is not a destination: name the file inside it.

frames.description: In one pass of the clip

shown.description: Frames shown since it started, every loop

powered.description: Whether the panel is awake; it sleeps whenever it shows nothing

path.description: A QuickTime Motion-JPEG clip (`.mov`), or a PNG, baseline JPEG or GIF

loop.description: A clip or animation: play it forever

whole_frame.description: Decode each frame whole, rather than streamed in blocks

loops.description: A clip or animation: play it this many times. Without `loop` or `loops`, a clip plays once and an animated GIF as the file says.

colour.description: `#rrggbb`, `rrggbb`, `R,G,B`, or a name: black, white, red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, orange, purple, pink, grey

kind.description: By the name's extension: `.mov` a clip, `.gif` an animation, `.png` and `.jpg` an image. An animation may turn out to have one frame.

mode.description: `wipe` lights each LED in turn to the colour; `rainbow` turns the colour wheel round the ring -- played once, either ends `off`. `flicker` flickers the colour like a failing hologram, until something else.

colour.description: For `solid`, `wipe` and `flicker` (white if never given). `#rrggbb`, `rrggbb`, `R,G,B`, or a name: black, white, red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, orange, purple, pink, grey

why.description: Why it cannot move, when it cannot

stopped.description: Why the last motion ended early, if it did

motion.description: `center`, `move` and `nudge` go to a place; `twitch` (random glances) and `scan` (a slow sweep) run until stopped or for `time_s`; `wag`, `nod` and `circle` run `count` times and return. `stop` holds where it is; `off` also lets the axes go limp.

x.description: `move`: -100..100, percent of the way from the centre to an endpoint, + right. `nudge`: -200..200, relative.

duration_ms.description: `center`, `move`, `nudge`: how long to take; by default, by the distance

range.description: Percent of the travel each side of the centre. Defaults: twitch 60, scan 70, wag 50, nod 40, circle 50.

period_ms.description: `wag` 700, `nod` 800, `circle` 2400 a turn, `scan` 6000 a sweep there and back

interval_s.description: `twitch`: the pause between glances, [min, max]; default [1, 5]

closed.description: At the closed end of the working range (the first 2% of travel): keep driving once settled, or let go

settle_ms.description: How long a command is driven before a `release` takes effect (at least 100)

abs_min_us.description: The most any command may send

calibrated.description: Whether the working range was saved, rather than the firmware's default

gpio.description: For a servo driven from a pin

us.description: The last pulse commanded; 0 before any

driven.description: Whether pulses are going out now

released.description: Whether the drive policy is what stopped them

us.description: A pulse width, within the absolute limits

then.description: When the scene ends: `stay` leaves everything as it is; `restore` puts the screen, LEDs and holo back to what they were doing before the scene -- a behaviour such as a twitch starts again; `off` turns the screen and LEDs off and lets the holo's servos go limp. Anything but `stay` needs the scene to end: `duration_s`, or a clip or animation on the screen that does not `loop` (in such a scene, one with neither `loop` nor `loops` plays once).

duration_s.description: The scene ends after this long, or when its clip has played if that is sooner

slot.description: A number for the scene, for the host link's native frames and small controllers, which apply it by number instead of by name. Unique: two scenes can't share one. *Planned: not in the firmware yet.*

Scene.description: Each part is optional: a part left out leaves that alone. A scene with only `leds` is an LED preset. A scene ends when its clip has played (once, or its `loops`), or after `duration_s`; `then` is what happens next. Applying another scene, or showing something else in place of its clip, ends it without `then`.

active.description: The scene running to its end, with a `then` to do when it gets there

scene.description: Applied without saving it; its name is not checked against the saved ones

boot_scene.description: The scene applied at every start; null: the screen and LEDs start off

brightness.description: Keep it at 30 or below when the strip is powered from the board

count.description: LEDs on the strip. Takes effect at the next start.

restart_required.description: A change that takes effect only at the next start is waiting for one

last.description: The one joined last, which the board rejoins at start

ssid.description: The name it has when on

off_in_s.description: On for a while (it came on because the board couldn't join a network at start, or from the BOOT button): seconds until it turns itself off. Absent when it stays on

sta_enabled.description: Whether the board joins networks at all. Off, a board reached over the network is lost until it is turned back on from the console or the access point.

networks.description: Strongest first; one entry an SSID

passphrase.description: Leave it out for an open network
Leave it out to use the saved one, or for an open network

on.description: Now only: the access point is off at every start, unless the board can't join a network then. `true` also keeps one that is on for a while on

cors.description: The sites whose pages may call the API: `https://host`, or `https://*.host` for any subdomain

hostname.description: The `.local` name; null for the default

password.description: Null to clear it. Never read back.

cors.description: The whole list; `[]` for none, null for the default

until_clip_ends.description: It ends when its clip has played

remaining_s.description: Until its `duration_s` is up; null without one

slot.description: Its slot, when it has one. *Planned: not in the firmware yet.*

Happening.description: Something that happened. `seq` numbers happenings from 1, going back to 1 after 65535, so a gap is a missed one (among the kinds a client follows, a gap means one of another kind, or a missed one: `?after=` with its `kinds` says which); the board keeps the last 32. Its other fields depend on `event` (ClipEnded, SceneEnded, Touch). A client ignores events and fields it doesn't know.

t_ms.description: The board's uptime when it happened, in milliseconds

path.description: From the root of the volume

finished.description: It played to its end; false when something replaced or stopped it

then.description: What it does at its end

by.description: `clip`: its clip played; `time`: its `duration_s` was up; `end`: `POST /scenes/end`; `replaced`: another scene or clip took over, and its `then` was not done

slot.description: The scene's slot, when it has one. *Planned: not in the firmware yet.*

SceneEnded.description: A scene running to its end (one with a `then`) ended

Touch.description: The screen was touched, or let go; only while touch reporting is on (`touch on`)

StateEvent.description: A resource changed: `state` is what its GET returns now. `screen`: ScreenState; `leds`: LedState; `holo`: HoloState, four times a second at most while it moves; `scene`: the running scene (SceneList.active), or null; `scenes`: the saved scenes (SceneList.scenes); `settings`: Settings; `network`: Network; `ota`: the update session (Ota.session), each second at most while an image arrives; `system`: {uptime_s, heap_free, rssi}, every 15 s. While a clip plays or a scene runs to its end, `screen` and `scene` are also sent every 5 s (CONFIG_WEBUI_EVENTS_SYNC_S), for clients counting frames or time on by themselves to sync to. Changes close together are sent as one, the latest; states are not kept, so a client that reconnects reads them again.

seq.description: The latest happening's number; 0 for none yet

kinds.description: The events the link reports: happenings, and resources whose changes are pushed (UART, with `push`). `[]` for none

push.description: Send them as they happen (UART only), or keep them for the host to fetch

LinkSettings.description: The link's saved settings. `mode`, `pins`, `attn`, `i2c_address` and `general_call` take effect at the next restart; the rest at once.

protocol.description: What UART and RS485 accept: JSON lines, native frames, or either (`auto`, told apart by the first byte). I2C is always `native`

pins.description: The GPIOs for the three roles: A is TX or SDA, B is RX or SCL, C is ATTN, DE or IRQ

baud.description: UART and RS485; 8N1, no flow control

address.description: The board's address on UART and RS485

groups.description: The groups it acts for, on UART and RS485

reply_delay_ms.description: RS485: how long it waits before answering, for the host's transceiver to stop sending

attn.description: UART: role C is an ATTN output, low while events are waiting

general_call.description: I2C: act on commands written to address 0

events.description: What the link reports from the start, until the host asks for something else

LinkPatch.description: Only what changes. The link's saved settings. `mode`, `pins`, `attn`, `i2c_address` and `general_call` take effect at the next restart; the rest at once.

protocol.description: What UART and RS485 accept: JSON lines, native frames, or either (`auto`, told apart by the first byte). I2C is always `native`

pins.description: The GPIOs for the three roles: A is TX or SDA, B is RX or SCL, C is ATTN, DE or IRQ

baud.description: UART and RS485; 8N1, no flow control

address.description: The board's address on UART and RS485

groups.description: The groups it acts for, on UART and RS485

reply_delay_ms.description: RS485: how long it waits before answering, for the host's transceiver to stop sending

attn.description: UART: role C is an ATTN output, low while events are waiting

general_call.description: I2C: act on commands written to address 0

events.description: What the link reports from the start, until the host asks for something else

bad_lines.description: JSON lines that didn't parse, or were too long

crc_errors.description: Native frames dropped for a bad CRC

framing_errors.description: Bytes received damaged: a wrong baud rate, or noise

overruns.description: Bytes lost because the host sent faster than the board read

seq.description: The latest happening's number on the board (shared with GET /events); 0 for none yet

pending.description: Happenings of these kinds not yet given to the host

running.description: What is running now, which differs from `settings` until a restart

restart_required.description: A saved change waits for a restart

last_request_s.description: Seconds since the last request over the link; null for none since the start
